A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeFacto research. All supplied pages, including figures, tables, equations and references, support comparison. Neither PDF contains appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original DeFacto benchmark results, training ablations and evidence-grounding evaluations in Tables 1–4 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark and ablation results, plus additional benchmark comparisons and counterfactual robustness results in Tables 3 and 5.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the specified no-evidence bbox output from unknown to null. The masking pipeline, three training views, backbone and custom rewards remain. Section 3.3 also revises the stated GRPO objective, but the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects changed implementation or corrected documentation.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluations on OCRBench, MMStar, MMMU, MMB 1.1 and POPE, extending coverage to additional OCR, multimodal reasoning and hallucination benchmarks. Table 5 also adds masked-evidence and whole-image-replacement test scenarios. The shortened training-source list does not establish that training datasets were removed.

E2.justification: New Table 3 adds reported comparisons against GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-Pro, Chain-of-Focus and Pixel Reasoner, alongside retained comparators DeepEyes and Visual-SR1. This substantially expands the evaluated comparison methods, including closed-source models. Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 5 introduces procedures that mask human-annotated evidence or replace the image, measuring abstention alongside categorized grounding/answer errors. This extends the evaluation protocol within DeFacto-1.5K. Existing training settings and the stated sampling of 100 examples per benchmark remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 5 quantitatively examines the three failure categories previously illustrated qualitatively in Figure 1, and tests robustness to evidence masking and image replacement against DeepEyes and GRIT. These directly investigate spurious correctness and evidence-dependent abstention. Existing training ablations remain, with revised full-model results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The standard deviation introduced in v3's GRPO advantage formula normalizes training rewards; it is not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise all 15 DeFacto scores while retaining comparator scores: for example, SciQA changes from 92.3 to 83.6, DocVQA from 86.8 to 94.0, and DeepForm from 63.7 to 45.6. Ablation results also change. v2 Table 4's mAP/AP50/AP75 values of 29.3/43.9/29.7 become 35.5/49.8/35.0 in v3 Table 6, matching unchanged Figure 3. New Tables 3 and 5 add benchmark, failure-rate and abstention results. These are reported revisions and additions, without an explanation establishing a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 9 gives a trajectory-level probability-ratio objective with mean-centered rewards. v3 Equations 9–11 replace it with a token-level clipped objective, KL regularization and advantages normalized by group reward standard deviation. This is a localized substantive mathematical revision; the remaining MDP and custom reward definitions are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central DeFacto, DeFacto-100K and DeFacto-1.5K contributions remain. The new conclusion explicitly claims the first vision-language reasoning framework grounded in counterfactual supervision. Meanwhile, Section 4.2 narrows general-VQA superiority from all six benchmarks and universal reported state-of-the-art to best performance on four of six.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new abstention tests as confirming dependence on visual evidence rather than language priors. Its new conclusion explicitly identifies detector errors, modest training-data scale and evaluation restricted to static images as limitations, with video and temporal reasoning left open. These qualifications were absent from v2.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces the explicit list of 16 training-data sources with three examples followed by 'among others,' reducing provenance detail without establishing a dataset change. The abstract also replaces separate code and direct Hugging Face dataset links with one GitHub code/data pointer. Hardware and numerical training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a substantial counterfactual-reasoning discussion distinguishing data generation from inference-based approaches, covering works such as CounterCurate, Counterfactual VQA, CRIPP-VQA, CFMM and MM-Verify. It also adds PAPO and TreeVGR to grounding-related positioning and removes the InternVL discussion and several references. This meaningfully expands the treatment of closely related research.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized abstract, output-format and results-discussion edits, shortens the training-source paragraph, and adds a related-work subsection, conclusion, impact statement and conflict disclosure. Author affiliations and correspondence information also change. The main section sequence and much of the existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds two compact tables, numbered 3 and 5. The former ablation Tables 3 and 4 become Tables 4 and 6, with the latter relocated. All three figures and existing table structures are retained. Equations are more tightly compressed on pages 5–6, and surrounding text reflows, without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Table 5 supplies more direct evidence for the central faithfulness claim, the new conclusion states concrete limitations, and Table 6 resolves the earlier disagreement with Figure 3's grounding totals. These improve empirical support and internal consistency. The overall gain is limited by reduced training-source disclosure, sparse descriptions of the new intervention protocols and unexplained revisions to existing benchmark scores.
